highlights: Zentro's core goes open source (GPL-3.0) with a 30-day Pro trial, plus a new Activity/Jobs panel, a much bigger AI assistant with MCP tools, SSH tunneling, an in-app terminal, and a keyboard-navigation overhaul.
body:
### Breaking Changes

- Pro Early Access is gone, replaced by a 30-day free trial of Pro available to everyone — no invite needed.

### New Features

- **Zentro's core is now open source** — the SQL IDE core ships under GPL-3.0-only; Pro stays a separate, licensed layer on top. See the README for what that means for building from source.
- **30-day Pro trial** — start it from Settings or any upgrade prompt; no credit card, and Upgrade to Pro now opens a real checkout session instead of just the pricing page.
- **Activity panel and background jobs** — long-running work (CSV import, full-table export) now runs as a cancelable job with live progress, instead of blocking the UI; a new Jobs tab tracks them, and a Server Sessions tab lists and can kill sessions on the database itself.
- **AI assistant, much further along** — a redesigned chat panel with saved history, streaming replies, and mention shortcuts; the assistant can now validate SQL, explain query plans, diff schemas across environments, find what breaks from a change, and read table/index stats, all gated to the schema it's allowed to see (ADR 0017) and fully free to use with your own model key, including the MCP server for external agents.
- **SSH tunnel and TLS controls per connection** — reach a database through an SSH tunnel, and set a minimum TLS version or allow legacy ciphers when a server needs them. The connection form also takes a connection string per driver (`postgres://`, `mysql://`, `sqlserver://`), with the right examples and defaults for each.
- **In-app terminal** — a local or SSH terminal lives in the bottom panel next to Activity and AI chat.
- **ERD improvements** — automatic layout (dagre), a minimap, keyboard pan/zoom, and a reset-layout control.
- **SQL editor polish** — its own SQL grammar so custom token colors always win over Monaco's defaults, schema-aware coloring of tables/columns/aliases, a redesigned Colors settings page with live preview, and a T-SQL-aware formatter.
- **Keyboard navigation overhaul** — roving-tabindex through the explorer tree and result grid, command-palette tab-jump, chord shortcuts, and Enter/F2 to start editing a cell.
- **Ctrl+Tab goes to your last tab** — it now switches to the most recently used tab, and holding Ctrl while pressing Tab walks further back, like a browser. Next/previous tab moved to Ctrl+PageDown / Ctrl+PageUp.
- **First-run product tours and a daily tip dialog** for new installs.

### Fixes & Polish

- **Security:** paid plans are now granted only from a verified signed entitlement, and the `ZENTRO_DEV_TIER` test override can no longer leak into a release build.
- AI: fixed empty/streaming replies on providers that ignore streaming, a stuck-reply timeout, and the chat model picker staying visible during setup.
- Activity: fixed an infinite re-render loop in the status-bar job indicator and incorrect export progress percentages.
- Result grid: drag-select survives missed mouse events, and copying a row selected via the index column works again.
- Shortcuts: chord completions now correctly win over single-key rules sharing a key, and Alt combos work on macOS.
- About now shows the real build commit and date on release builds.
- Sessions tab no longer lists Postgres's own background workers.
- Connection form: the SSL mode and TLS version lists open above the dialog again, and Test / Cancel / Save stay pinned at the bottom instead of scrolling away.
- The command palette closes when you click outside it, not only on Esc.
- The assistant's run-history tools now stay off until you turn on **Run history** in Settings → Assistant, as the setting says.

highlights: Smarter SQL editing with live diagnostics, safer row deletes, native Linux/macOS installers, and a full theme token overhaul.
body:
### New Features

- **Live SQL diagnostics** — the editor now flags unknown columns and ambiguous references as errors inline (Error Lens style) as you type, with did-you-mean, qualify, and refresh quick fixes, and a Settings toggle to turn it off.
- **Smarter completion** — suggestions are now dialect-aware, qualify columns by alias in multi-table joins, offer `alias.*`/`All columns` expansions, pull in foreign-key related columns with the LEFT JOIN they need, and write long select lists comma-first, one column per line. `Expand *` and a quick Run command (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) round it out.
- **Safer deletes** — deleting or dropping rows now shows which other tables actually reference them, lets you view those referencing rows before confirming, and only warns when a real reference exists.
- **Query results, unsaved-edit aware** — re-running a query keeps a result tab's unsaved edits instead of discarding them, and F5/reload now honours the active filter and asks before dropping unsaved changes.
- **One Messages/Summary tab per run** — server messages (including MSSQL `PRINT`/`RAISERROR` output) collect into a single Messages tab, and multi-statement non-SELECT runs get one Summary tab instead of one per statement.
- **Smoother scrolling** — mouse-wheel scrolling is eased across the query editor, result grid, and tab bars.
- **PII blur is now a real guard** — blurring sensitive columns when presenting actually prevents exposure instead of only being a visual effect.
- **Native installers for Linux and macOS** — Linux ships as `.deb`, `.rpm` (Fedora), and AppImage (with zsync auto-update and bundled GTK3/WebKit2GTK) in place of the raw binary/tarball; macOS gets an ad-hoc signed `.pkg` installer with auto-update.
- **Theme system rebuilt** — Button components now use a dedicated token layer with an accent rebrand, and Solarized Light gets its own primary color instead of borrowing Dark's blue.
- **Faster project switching** — new connections can be added directly from the environment picker, and first-time Project creation is gated on a privacy notice.

### Fixes & Polish

- Explorer: working reconnect button, virtualized object list, debounced filter, and no more duplicate concurrent schema fetches or cascading query failures on reconnect.
- Result grid: correct drag-select column ranges, immediate column auto-fit on double-click, and cell editors that re-render on every keystroke.
- Theme: full token architecture overhaul (Seed → Map → Alias, `danger`/`error` renamed to `destructive`) with parity fixes across all four built-in presets, and multiple Solarized contrast/selection fixes.
- Editor: builtin SQL snippets insert as real Monaco snippets, fonts re-measure once the webfont loads so the caret lines up, and query/table tabs stop re-rendering on unrelated actions.
- SQL generation: correct N-prefixed unicode strings for SQL Server, escaped backslashes for MySQL, and Postgres dollar-quoted bodies kept as one statement.
- MSSQL: batch-scoped statements stay together and PRINT output is no longer dropped when throttled.
- Autosave no longer writes on every keystroke; table columns fetch once instead of three times.
- Toolbar shows a sweeping progress bar while connecting instead of a pulse, and stays in sync when the active connection is edited elsewhere.
- Update dialog redesigned and no longer shows the wrong current version.
- Stray console windows removed, data-grid selection UX cleaned up, and F1/keyboard-shortcut help added.

highlights: Windows auto-update no longer strands the app on a closed window — a detached helper now owns the whole download-and-install sequence and always relaunches
body:
### New Features

- **Reworked Windows auto-update** — the old flow downloaded the update inside the running app, then quit and re-ran the installer via a hidden PowerShell one-liner; a real subset of failures left you staring at a closed app with no relaunch. Auto-update now spawns a small detached helper (its own window and tray icon) that takes over once the app quits: it waits for the app to fully exit, downloads the release with visible progress, verifies its checksum, runs the installer elevated and silent, then relaunches Zentro. Every path through the helper ends in a relaunch — even a failed install won't strand you without the app — and Zentro reports whether the update succeeded the next time it starts.

### Fixes & Polish

- The update modal and toolbar update button were simplified to match the new single-step flow: the modal's call-to-action now reads "Restart & Install" on Windows and triggers the restart directly, and the toolbar button dropped its now-obsolete downloading/restart-staged states.

highlights: A dedicated Connections page in Settings, connection creation during first-run onboarding, and stable connection identity so a connection can be renamed without breaking its project bindings or saved password
body:
### Breaking Changes

- **An unbound project environment now errors instead of silently connecting to the pool's bootstrap database.** Previously, an environment with no database of its own fell back to the connection's `db_name`. That fallback is gone — the database a project works against lives only on the environment binding. The upgrade backfills every existing environment from its connection so nothing you already use breaks; but a *new* environment with no database picked will now report a clear "unbound" error rather than connecting somewhere unexpected.

### New Features

- **Settings → Connections** — a dedicated page that is now the single place to manage the connection pool: create, edit, test, and delete connections, list and create databases per connection, and import or export them (moved here from the project dialog). Deleting a connection tells you how many project environments across how many projects still use it.
- **Create a connection during first-run onboarding** — a fresh install with an empty pool can now add its first connection inline from the startup project wizard, instead of hitting a dead end that required restarting the app. The provider picker — choose Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, and the rest by its logo — is back on both the onboarding flow and the Settings page.
- **Stable connection identity** — every pool connection now has a permanent ID. Renaming a connection no longer orphans the project environments bound to it or the password saved in your OS keyring. This also fixes a reported bug where picking a different database in a project's environment matrix still connected to the previous one.
- **The environment matrix is now a pure binder** — it picks a connection and a database, nothing more; all connection editing routes to Settings → Connections. Rebinding the database of the environment you're currently connected to now reconnects the live session and tells you what happened, and merely opening a picker while editing a project no longer switches your connected environment when you save.
- **Live project names and colours in the connection list** — the "used by" column reads project names and identity colours from the live project store, so a project renamed elsewhere updates here immediately instead of after a restart. A new **Refresh** button reloads connections, database probes, and bindings together.
- **Per-database bindings view** — expanding a connection now shows two columns: every database (including ones a project references but the server no longer has, flagged "not on server") and the project environments bound to each.

### Fixes & Polish

- **Toolbar centre content is actually centred on the window** — an asymmetric inset that reserved the corner for the window controls was pulling the centre cluster about 69px off true centre; the chrome insets moved onto the side clusters instead.
- Internal cleanup: removed the last of the inline connection-CRUD code from the project dialog and environment matrix, and made every frontend call site resolve a project's connection reference by ID rather than by display name.

highlights: One shared connection pool across every project, a redesigned project wizard, theme presets and font settings, a built-in update button, and a broad UI refresh
body:
### Breaking Changes

- **Connections are now a single global pool.** Connections used to be stored inside each project. They now live in one shared pool, and each project environment points to a pool connection plus the database it's bound to. Your existing connections are folded into the pool automatically the first time you launch v0.6.0 — deduplicated by driver / host / port / database / user, with saved passwords carried over. No action needed, but a connection you set up in one project is now visible to all of them.
- Connection export/import now uses a `{ version, connections: [] }` bundle (secrets are always stripped). The old single-connection package can still be imported.

### New Features

- **Redesigned project wizard** — create and edit projects through a new profile dialog with an Environment Matrix picker for wiring each environment to a connection, a quick-switch context menu, a teal default project colour, and a responsive layout
- **Quick project switcher** — jump between projects straight from the toolbar, with full keyboard navigation
- **Theme presets and fonts** — pick a built-in preset (Zentro Light, Zentro Dark, or Solarized) and set separate font families for the UI and the SQL editor, all from Settings
- **Built-in update button** — the update check is now always on and no longer configurable (VS Code style). When a newer release is available, a compact **Update** / **Restart to Update** button appears in the toolbar; hover it to see your current version and the latest one. No more auto-popup modal.
- **Extensible bottom panel** — the editor's bottom panel is now a registry hosting Audit, Output, App Log, and Query Stats, with room for more over time
- **VS Code-style empty editor state** — a cleaner starting screen for a new query tab, with a right-sidebar resizer that stays in sync
- **Data grid zebra striping** — alternating row shading and header dividers that hold up while scrolling
- **Broad UI redesign** — unified panel borders and corner radii, resizable sidebars, a boxed settings navigation, and a refreshed tab strip and result panel; the first-run window can now be dragged by the dialog background

### Fixes & Polish

- The light/dark switch in Settings now applies on the first click, and changing the theme no longer wipes the font/preset fields on save
- Consistent panel divider across every theme; the active tab now has a surface distinct from the tab strip; Solarized presets match the canonical palette
- Edited cells now generate provider-correct SQL literals
- The result panel only auto-opens for real editor query runs, not background queries
- Log views no longer re-theme every open Monaco editor
- `time.Time` values render in a single canonical form instead of Go's doubled timezone
- Context Search: table tabs opened from the palette stay pinned to the toolbar context, and the list resets scroll and selects the first row on every new query
- Window controls stay pinned to the top-right corner, and every dialog has rounded corners
- The "no connection" notice is debounced so switching projects doesn't flash it
- Typing in the editor feels immediate again — the Monaco-to-store sync is debounced — and the result grid stays smooth under fast scrolling
